title: Secure Coding Practices for .NET & React AI Applications
description: Defend against SQL injection, XSS in streaming markdown, SSRF in agent web tools, and secure deserialization in .NET.

data.text: Defensive Engineering in the Full-Stack AI Era

Building AI applications with React and .NET creates unique full-stack security considerations. On the frontend, rendering dynamic streaming Markdown from an LLM can inadvertently introduce Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) if unverified HTML tags or script injection payloads are executed. On the backend, granting an agent the ability to fetch web URLs or query SQL databases can expose systems to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and SQL injection if parameters are not rigorously sanitized.
Preventing XSS in Streaming React Markdown

When rendering AI streaming tokens in React using libraries like react-markdown, an attacker could inject malicious script tags or JavaScript URI links (e.g. [Click Here](javascript:stealTokens())). Always pair markdown renderers with DOMPurify or rehype-sanitize.

data.text: Preventing SSRF in Agent Web Fetch Tools in C#

When building an agent with a 'browse_url' or 'fetch_webpage' tool, an attacker might submit prompts asking the model to fetch http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token (the cloud instance metadata service) or internal localhost ports (http://localhost:5000/admin). Your .NET tool must validate that target IPs are not private or link-local addresses.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Sanitize all rendered Markdown using rehype-sanitize and strict protocol whitelist rules
Prevent SSRF in agent browsing tools by validating DNS IPs against private subnets and metadata services
Always use parameterized queries (EF Core / Dapper parameters) when interacting with databases
Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to restrict image and script origin sources
Treat LLM tool outputs and streaming tokens with the same zero-trust scrutiny as untrusted user inputs
data.takeaway: Secure coding is the bedrock of reliable AI applications. Hardening React markdown rendering against XSS and .NET agent tools against SSRF prevents attackers from turning AI capabilities against your infrastructure.
